risks.description: As the first at-scale UK cement plant incorporating CCS, FOAK technical integration challenges could result in operational downtime or reduced capture efficiency.
risks.mitigation: Engage independent technical assurance (WSP) and implement rigorous stage-gate testing during commissioning and early operation.
risks.evidence: Section 1: Padeswood will be the first at-scale UK cement plant incorporating Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology

risks.description: Operational failures or outages in the connected HyNet T&S network could prevent Padeswood from offloading captured CO2, causing operational cross-chain disruption.
risks.mitigation: Utilize the Cluster Sponsor Function to manage cross-chain delivery risks and enforce Network Code operational compliance.

risks.description: Delayed deployment of CCUS could cause internationally owned parents to shift investment away from the UK due to carbon pricing, leading to carbon leakage.
risks.mitigation: Provide capital grant support via CIF and long-term revenue certainty via the ICC business model prior to UK CBAM implementation.
risks.evidence: Section 2.1.3: Without investment in CCUS, companies may de-prioritise their UK interests and shift production elsewhere where the cost is lower

risks.description: Misalignment with spurline construction timelines could delay project Final Investment Decision by 4 months and Commercial Operation Date by 5 months.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate spurline infrastructure delivery directly with HyNet cluster schedules through the Cluster Sponsor Function.
risks.evidence: Section 3.1: Padeswood Delayed: presents an alternative option where FID is delayed by 4 months to align with their spurline timelines

risks.description: Fluctuations in input energy prices and carbon market prices could lead to budget overruns and operational cost volatility.
risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous Open Book Model monitoring and utilize strike price adjustment mechanics within the ICC business model.

risks.description: Under-performance in captured volumes or low carbon prices could expand government support liabilities under the Revenue Support Agreement (RSA).
risks.mitigation: Structure the ICC contract with performance thresholds and safeguards against volume under-delivery administered by LCCC.

risks.description: Premature project cancellation or discontinuation would lead to stranded public capital grants and unrecovered private investments.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict conditions precedent before grant drawdown and establish clear termination provisions within commercial contracts.

risks.description: Default events or financial distress could trigger unexpected direct liabilities for the Exchequer under Secretary of State Direct Agreements.
risks.mitigation: Implement multi-body post-FID oversight via DESNZ CGL, LCCC, and Ofgem to continuously track counterparty financial stability.
risks.evidence: Section 5.4.3: Exchequer funding Secretary of State direct agreements (SoSDA)

risks.description: Inaccurate reporting or fraudulent claims during grant disbursements or operational revenue support payments could misallocate public funds.
risks.mitigation: Subject all financial claims to DESNZ Central Grants & Loans administration controls and independent Open Book auditing.

risks.description: Overlapping or unclear operational responsibilities among DESNZ, Ofgem, LCCC, and CGL could cause decision-making delays post-FID.
risks.mitigation: Implement the Post-FID Operating Model with explicit functional boundaries and centralize coordination in the Cluster Sponsor Function.
risks.evidence: Section 6.4: Managing government-owned cross-chain delivery risks and operating model integration risks.

risks.description: Business model subsidy structures could face legal challenge if found non-compliant with Energy and Environment principles regarding polluter obligations.
risks.mitigation: Ensure independent legal assurance (Ashurst) validates subsidy design against statutory Energy and Environment guidelines.
risks.evidence: Section 4.3: subsidies do not to relieve the beneficiary from liabilities as a polluter.

risks.description: Captured CO2 failing to meet standardized composition or physical state specifications could cause entry rejection by the T&S operator.
risks.mitigation: Design and operate capture facilities in strict adherence to standardized CCS Network Code parameters confirmed by technical assurance.
risks.evidence: Section 4.6: Padeswood is compliant with the CCS Network Code, which standardises technical and operational arrangements

risks.description: Delays or lower operational capture at Padeswood could leave HyNet T&S network capacity unutilized, reducing overall cluster Value for Money.
risks.mitigation: Monitor network utilization against project indicator frameworks and enforce minimum throughput requirements in operational agreements.
risks.evidence: Section 2.1.5: Padeswood provides an opportunity to increase the T&S network utilisation and therefore the value for money

risks.description: Escalating long-term nominal funding commitments across cluster projects could breach the £21.7bn Final Funding Envelope approved by HM Treasury.
risks.mitigation: Enforce continuous budget oversight and spending approval limits through DESNZ and HM Treasury governance frameworks.
risks.evidence: Section 5.2: In Autumn 2024, the Chancellor approved a Final Funding Envelope (FFE) of £21.7bn in Real 2021 prices
